headline: 16 Bangladeshis killed in devastating sofa factory fire in Saudi Arabia
summary: A massive fire engulfed a sofa factory in Riyadh's Musa Industrial Area, claiming the lives of at least 16 Bangladeshi nationals. Rescue operations were ongoing as authorities worked to identify the victims.
details: At least 16 Bangladeshi nationals were killed in a devastating fire at a sofa factory in Saudi Arabia. The incident occurred in the Musa Industrial Area under the Al-Shifa police station in Riyadh around 2:00 PM yesterday.
The Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry issued a notification confirming the deaths, quoting fire service personnel. Witnesses stated that all victims were from Bangladesh.

Rescue operations were still underway by the local fire service when the notification was issued around 1:30 AM today (Bangladesh time). The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh has expressed profound sorrow over the tragedy.
Officials from the Bangladesh Embassy are present at the site and are in close contact with Saudi authorities. Their primary focus is on identifying the victims and providing necessary support.
Earlier, Expatriates’ Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury had reported that seven Bangladeshi workers from Naogaon’s Atrai upazila were among those killed. The death toll was later updated to 16.

headline: SSC and equivalent exam results to be published today, August 10, for 1.85 million students
summary: Education Minister Dr. Anm Ehsanul Hoque Milan will inaugurate the results at 10 AM, ending the wait for over 1.85 million students across the country.
details: The wait for this year's SSC and equivalent examination results concludes today, Monday, August 10. Education Minister Dr. Anm Ehsanul Hoque Milan will inaugurate the results at 10 AM in a ceremony at the Ministry of Education conference room.

Students can access their results simultaneously online, through their educational institutions, and via mobile SMS. This information was confirmed in a Ministry of Education notification issued on Sunday, August 9.

According to the notification, chairmen of all education boards will hand over the results to the Education Minister during the inauguration ceremony. Professor Dr. Syed Akhtaruzzaman, Chairman of Dhaka Education Board and President of Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee, announced on Saturday that the results would be published concurrently at 10 AM today.

Results will be available on the respective education board websites, as well as two common websites: eduboardresult.gov.bd and educationboardresults.gov.bd. Students can also collect their results directly from their educational institutions.

To receive results via SMS, students need to type 'SSC' followed by a space, the first three letters of their board name, then their roll number, another space, and the exam year, sending it to 16140. For example, 'SSC DHA ROLL YEAR' for Dhaka Board.
The SMS format for Madrasa Board (Dakhil) is 'SSC MAD ROLL YEAR' and for Technical Board (SSC Vocational) is 'SSC TEC ROLL YEAR'. Each SMS will cost BDT 1.39, including all taxes.

A total of 1,857,344 students filled out forms for this year's SSC and equivalent examinations. This includes 1,418,398 students under nine general education boards, 304,286 for Dakhil under the Madrasa Education Board, and 134,660 for SSC (Vocational) under the Technical Education Board.
Applications for result re-scrutiny will be accepted online from August 11 to August 17. Instructions for the application process will be published on the education boards' websites.
Educational institutions can download and publish results from the designated website by using their board and EIIN in the 'Result' corner.
